 Springboks Change: Rassie Erasmus ‘takes A Cautious Approach’ As Star Withdraws From Ireland Clash 
 Springboks change: Rassie Erasmus ‘takes a cautious approach’ as star withdraws from Ireland clash
 Louis Chapman Coombe 
 20 Nov 2026 9:38 AM 
 Franco Mostert will start for the Springboks this weekend, after being promoted into the side. 
 The Springboks have been forced into a late change to their 23-man squad to face Ireland, with Ruan Nortje pulling out through injury. 
 Nortje was initially set to start alongside Eben Etzebeth in the second-row for the Boks’ Nations Championship showdown with the Irish, as they look to atone for their defeat in Paris last time out, but he has now withdrawn after picking up a knock in training.
 In his place, Franco Mostert comes straight into the run-on group at lock, with Lood de Jager remaining on the bench.
 Springboks forced into late change as Ruan Nortje withdraws through injury
 “Springbok utility forward Franco Mostert will start Saturday’s Nations Championship encounter against Ireland in Dublin at lock next to Eben Etzebeth following the withdrawal of Ruan Nortje on Friday due to a niggle picked up at training this week,” the Boks said in a statement.
 Andy Farrell bats away Rassie question but addresses Prendergast, Furlong and the ‘world’s leading’ scrum 
 “Nortje has been monitored by the Bok medical team throughout the week, but Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus opted to take a cautious approach on Friday morning, naming Mostert in the second-row to give Nortje further time to recover from his injury.”
 Utility man Mostert has come off the bench in both of the Boks’ Tests this month, but now makes his first start of the November Nations Championship block after his promotion into the side.
 Elsewhere, though, South Africa are as previously advertised from their team announcement earlier this week. Damian Willemse starts at full-back, with Kurt-Lee Arendse and Ethan Hooker on the wings.

 Jesse Kriel and Damian de Allende form the midfield partnership, while Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Morne van den Berg continue in the halves.
 Cameron Hanekom, Pieter-Steph du Toit and captain Siya Kolisi start in the back-row, with Mostert partnering the aforementioned Etzebeth in the locks. Wilco Louw, Malcolm Marx and Ox Nche form the run-on front-row.
 Nations Championship, Round Six: Teams, kick-off times, global TV channels and more 
 South Africa have also opted to run a 6:2 split on the bench, with Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp, Thomas du Toit, De Jager, Paul de Villiers, Marco van Staden, Grant Williams and Canan Moodie all included.
 Updated Springboks team in full
 Springboks: 15 Damian Willemse, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse, 13 Jesse Kriel, 12 Damian de Allende, 11 Ethan Hooker, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, 9 Morne van den Berg, 8 Cameron Hanekom, 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 6 Siya Kolisi (c), 5 Franco Mostert, 4 Eben Etzebeth, 3 Wilco Louw, 2 Malcolm Marx, 1 Ox Nche
 Replacements: 16 Jan-Hendrik Wessels, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Paul de Villiers, 21 Marco van Staden, 22 Grant Williams, 23 Canan Moodie
 Date: Saturday, 21 November 2026
 Venue: Aviva Stadium, Dublin
 Kick-off: 16:40 (local), 16:40 (UK), 17:40 (France), 18:40 (South Africa), 03:40 (22 November, AEDT), 05:40 (22 November, New Zealand), 13:40 (Argentina), 01:40 (22 November, JST), 11:40 (EST)
 Referee: Christophe Ridley (RFU)
 Assistant Referees: Angus Gardner (RA) and Anthony Woodthorpe (RFU)
 TMO: Ian Tempest (RFU)
 FPRO: Tual Trainini (FFR)
 Broadcasters: Virgin Media Television (Republic of Ireland), ITV / ITVX (United Kingdom), TF1 (France), SuperSport (South Africa / Africa), Sky Italia (Italy), Nine Network / Stan Sport (Australia), Sky Sport (New Zealand), FloSports (USA), Wowow (Japan)
